name: First steroid cycle

lead: A first steroid cycle is the first time someone uses anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) for a set period, usually to build muscle, leanness and a more V-shaped, masculine physique. 'First cycle' threads are a staple of lifting and looksmaxxing forums.

Wikipedia notes that most non-medical users are not competitive athletes but men, median age around 25, using the drugs for appearance. Forum threads typically ask members to review a planned stack, and replies add or change items.

paras: In forum posts a first cycle is described as a limited block of an injectable testosterone ester, sometimes with other compounds, followed by what users call post-cycle therapy to restore natural production. Threads combine it with training and diet. No protocol is given here.

Documented effects include unfavorable cholesterol changes, acne, high blood pressure, liver strain with oral forms, heart enlargement, gynecomastia, testicular shrinkage, reduced sperm production, temporary suppression of natural testosterone and mood changes. In adolescents, AAS can prematurely close growth plates. They are controlled substances in many countries.

chain: Steroids activate the androgen receptor and raise muscle protein synthesis
Faster muscle growth and shorter recovery between sessions
A larger, leaner, more muscular V-taper physique
angle.text: AAS increase muscle size and strength beyond what training alone typically produces in the same time, which is why lifters use them for physique change [1][9]. A first cycle is the entry point to that route, usually combined with heavy training and a calorie-controlled diet [4].

lead: A first steroid cycle is a person's first planned course of anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS), the testosterone-related drugs people use to gain muscle, strength and a leaner, broader, more masculine physique faster than training alone. 'Cycle' refers to the habit of using the drugs for a set block of weeks, stopping, and later repeating; the first one is the point at which a lifter moves from natural training to drug-assisted training [1][2].

The appearance logic is direct. AAS increase muscle protein synthesis, reduce muscle breakdown and shorten recovery, so a lifter can add more muscle mass, and with it shoulder, chest and arm size, than they otherwise would [1]. In a randomized trial, healthy men given high weekly testosterone doses for ten weeks while lifting gained more fat-free mass, muscle size and strength than men who lifted without the drug [3]. Looksmaxxing forums frame it as a route to 'frame' and a V-shaped upper body.

The topic is one of the most common on looksmax.org, where members post planned compound lists, age, height and goals and ask others to critique them [4][5][6]. Beyond forums, steroid use among non-competitive lifters has been documented by medical bodies and journalists; the Endocrine Society notes that most users are recreational weightlifters rather than athletes [7], and a 2023 advocacy-group report counted hundreds of millions of TikTok views of videos promoting steroid-like drugs [8].

AAS are controlled substances in the United States (Schedule III), the United Kingdom (Class C), Canada (Schedule IV) and many other countries [1]. Medical bodies describe documented cardiovascular, hormonal, hepatic and psychiatric risks, and in adolescents the possibility of premature growth-plate closure [1][7][2]. This article describes the practice and what people say and research reports about it; it does not give protocols.

paras: A cycle is a defined period of AAS use followed by a break. NIDA defines the surrounding vocabulary: cycling is taking multiple doses over a period, stopping, and starting again; stacking is combining two or more steroids, often oral and injectable; and pyramiding is a pattern of gradually rising and then tapering use over roughly six to twelve weeks. The agency adds that none of these patterns has been scientifically validated [2].

The first cycle is the user's introduction. In forum posts it is usually described as simpler than later ones, built around a single injectable testosterone ester, though the plans posted range widely and sometimes include growth hormone, GLP-1-type drugs, thyroid hormone and protective drugs [6][4]. Posts typically state age, height, weight and body-fat estimates, so that other members can comment on the plan.

Medically, AAS are prescribed for delayed puberty, hypogonadism, muscle-wasting diseases and burns. Non-medical doses reported in the literature can be many times the medical range [1][2]. Injection is the most common route among non-medical users, with orals used for shorter blocks [1].

Testosterone was identified in 1935 by a group of researchers around Ernst Laqueur, and Adolf Butenandt and Leopold Ruzicka published syntheses the same year; the two chemists were offered the 1939 Nobel Prize in Chemistry [1]. Human trials began in 1937 [1].

Eastern Bloc weightlifting programs adopted steroids from the 1940s onward. After Soviet lifters' success, US team physician John Ziegler worked on a derivative with fewer androgenic effects, producing metandienone (Dianabol), approved by the FDA in 1958; off-label users were mostly bodybuilders and weightlifters [1]. In bodybuilding, significant use is associated with the late 1960s and early 1970s, with figures such as Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sergio Oliva and Lou Ferrigno, and use was discussed openly during the 1970s partly because the drugs were legal [9].

The International Olympic Committee banned anabolic steroids in 1976 and later introduced out-of-competition testing [1]. After Ben Johnson's 1988 Olympic scandal, the US Congress passed the Anabolic Steroids Control Act of 1990, placing steroids in Schedule III, and a 2004 act added prohormones effective January 2005 [1]. Several pharmaceutical companies stopped marketing steroids in the US in the early 1990s [1].

sections.h: Origins and spread in online culture
paras: Forum 'first cycle' threads are a recurring genre. On looksmax.org, titles include 'first cycle at 15 for height frame maxxing', 'first cycle frame growth' and 'first cycle advice', and authors range from late teens to twenties [10][11][12]. Replies commonly propose additions, such as hair-loss or liver-support products, or comment on the cycle's length [4][5]. T Nation, a long-running lifting forum, treats the phrase as a running joke as well as a topic: one thread quotes advice not to start a first cycle without knowing how to train, followed by the reply that it is not the poster's first [13].

Outside forums, advocacy and media attention has focused on social platforms. A 2023 report by the Center for Countering Digital Hate found that TikTok videos under hashtags promoting steroid-like drugs drew more than 580 million views from US users over three years, mostly from men aged 18 to 24. The report identified 35 influencers tied to sales websites and with about 1.8 million combined followers, some earning commissions through affiliate links; it also described a teenage-bodybuilding account making claims about height [8]. The organisation's chief executive said the findings showed a 'stark failure' of platform enforcement; TikTok disputed the report's methodology [8]. A Wikipedia summary notes a 2023 study of 20 influencers promoting performance-enhancing substances, three of whom had more than one million followers [9].

Practitioners say a first cycle accelerates the 'natural limit' of muscle gain, gives faster recovery so more training volume is possible, and produces a leaner, harder look. Forum users also discuss 'frame' and height goals, in some posts for teenagers, along with plans to add growth hormone [10][11].

Researchers and medical bodies describe the muscle effect as well supported and the height claim as the opposite: AAS can close growth plates early and limit adult height in adolescents [1][2]. A recurring community belief is that a short course followed by agents such as clomifene or hCG returns natural testosterone to normal; Wikipedia states that short courses of one to two months typically return natural production to normal with such therapy [1].

In the 1996 randomized trial by Bhasin and colleagues, 43 healthy men were assigned to placebo or 600 mg weekly testosterone enanthate, with or without a weight-lifting program, for ten weeks. Testosterone alone increased muscle size and strength relative to placebo, the combination with exercise produced the largest gains, and mood and behavior did not change in any group [3].

For harms, researchers rely on observational data because trials cannot ethically reproduce typical non-medical doses and drug combinations. A 2014 Endocrine Society scientific statement linked performance-enhancing drug use to increased mortality and to cardiovascular, psychiatric, metabolic, endocrine, neurologic, hepatic, renal and musculoskeletal problems, and noted that users often take doses far above physiologic levels and combine drugs [7]. A 2017 cross-sectional study of 140 male weightlifters aged 34 to 54, 86 of them long-term users, found lower left ventricular ejection fraction in users (52% vs 63%), impaired diastolic function in both current and former users, and more coronary plaque linked to lifetime duration of use; the authors cautioned that the design shows association, not causation [14]. Studies of users who stop report that systolic function largely normalised off drug [14].

NIDA reports that steroids do not produce a euphoric high but can lead to a steroid use disorder, with one review estimating about 32% of misusers become dependent, and that withdrawal can include fatigue, insomnia, reduced sex drive and depression [2].

Documented effects include unfavorable cholesterol changes, high blood pressure, left ventricular enlargement, heart attack, stroke and sudden cardiac death; liver damage mainly with oral forms; kidney changes; acne; gynecomastia; testicular shrinkage; reduced sperm production and infertility, which is often reversible; and mood effects such as aggression, mania and depression [1][2]. The IARC classes AAS as probably carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A) [1]. Non-sterile or shared injection equipment carries infection risk [2]. In women and children, effects such as voice deepening can be irreversible [1][2]. In adolescents, premature growth-plate closure can stunt growth, and NIDA adds that adolescent exposure may affect brain development [2].

AAS are Schedule III in the United States, Schedule IV in Canada and Class C in the UK [1]. Where they are controlled, supply is through smuggled, clandestine or counterfeit products [1]. Most sporting bodies ban them [1].

No studies of 'first cycles' as a category have been published. Randomized trials of testosterone in healthy men show gains in muscle size and strength [3], and observational studies of long-term users document cardiac and vascular changes [14][7].

lore.intro: First-cycle threads on looksmax.org present a planned stack and invite critique, often from teenagers and early twenties, and similar content circulates on lifting forums and short-video platforms [4][5][8].

claims.claim: A first cycle adds muscle and a better physique quickly
A first cycle at 15-17 can add height or frame growth
Side effects are manageable with blood work and add-on drugs
Steroids are easy to run safely when influencers do it

timeline.event: Testosterone is identified and synthesised by competing European teams [1].
Human clinical trials of methyltestosterone and testosterone propionate begin [1].
The FDA approves metandienone (Dianabol), popular with bodybuilders off-label [1].
Steroid use is openly discussed in bodybuilding; Pumping Iron appears in 1977 [9].
The US Anabolic Steroids Control Act places steroids in Schedule III [1].
Bhasin and colleagues publish the NEJM trial of testosterone with and without exercise [3].
US prohormone controls from the 2004 act take effect [1].
Endocrine Society scientific statement on adverse effects of performance-enhancing drugs is published [7].
Baggish et al. report cardiac and coronary findings in long-term users [14].
CCDH reports hundreds of millions of TikTok views of videos promoting steroid-like drugs [8].
